title: Guardrails gating: make metric ordering deterministic + validate gating metrics schema
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Fix flaky Optimize guardrails gating outcomes caused by non-deterministic metric ordering; add schema validation to fail fast on malformed/duplicated metric keys.
body:
Context: During pilot we saw intermittent gating flips (pass/fail) for identical inputs. Root cause: the policy engine built the per-suite metric map from an upstream JSON object where iteration order was not stable across languages/serialization paths, and our decision logic accidentally depended on that order in two places: (1) summary hashing for cached eval results and (2) threshold evaluation loop that used first-match semantics when duplicate metric keys existed.

This PR makes gating decisions deterministic and adds explicit schema validation for the metric payload produced by eval-harness “gating mode”.

What changed: 1) Canonical metric ordering: Normalize gating metrics to a stable, sorted order before decision evaluation and before computing cache keys/audit summaries. Sorting is by (metric_name, slice_key, aggregator) with a stable tie-breaker on “source” when present. 2) Schema validation: Add a lightweight validator that runs at the control-plane boundary (Optimize apply -> policy engine) to enforce: - metric_name must be present and match our taxonomy regex ([a-z0-9_\.]+) - no duplicate metric_name + slice_key + aggregator triples - numeric fields must be finite (no NaN/Inf) - optional CI bounds must satisfy low <= mean <= high when present - required fields for gating mode: prompt_set_revision, suite_id, model_id, model_version - reject unknown aggregator values early (only mean/p50/p90/pass_rate supported in gating)

Why this fixes flakiness: The policy engine’s decision function is now a pure function of a canonicalized payload. Duplicate metric keys are now a hard error (previously “last write wins” or “first match wins” depending on traversal order).

Implementation notes: - Added `canonicalizeMetrics()` in policy-engine utils and used it in both `evaluateThresholds()` and `computeGatingSummaryHash()`.
- Validator returns a structured failure reason surfaced to the caller as `GATING_INPUT_INVALID` (no retry). This is distinct from `EVAL_RUN_TIMEOUT` and `EVAL_RUN_FAILED`.
- Added regression tests that run the same metrics in randomized orders across 100 iterations to ensure stable decision outputs.

Illustrative snippet (policy-engine):

Before:
- for (const [name, metric] of Object.entries(metrics)) { ... }

After:
- for (const metric of canonicalizeMetrics(metrics)) { ... }

Testing: - Unit: `policy-engine/determinism.test.ts` validates stable decision + stable summary hash across permutations. - Unit: `policy-engine/metrics_schema_validation.test.ts` covers duplicates, bad aggregator, NaN, CI inconsistencies. - Integration: updated E2E apply-flow test to assert deterministic `gating_run_summary.hash`.

Operational impact: This should reduce noisy overrides and “rerun fixes it” behavior. In the rare case the payload is malformed (e.g., duplicated keys from an upstream bug), the apply will now fail with a clear, actionable error pointing at the offending metric triple.

Follow-ups (not included): - Add a counter metric for validation failures by suite_id (telemetry ticket tracked in ENG-3927). - Consider enforcing canonical ordering inside eval-harness output as defense-in-depth.

Screens/Logs: - Attached in CI artifacts: `determinism_permutation_log.txt` showing identical decisions/hashes across permutations.

Review checklist: - [x] Deterministic canonicalization and hashing - [x] Validation failures are non-retriable - [x] No behavior change for valid inputs (except determinism) - [x] Backwards compatible with existing gating output (only stricter on duplicates/NaN)

Conversation:

Selene Huang (review): Can we confirm this doesn’t change pass/fail for valid payloads? Also, what do we surface to Console when validation fails?

Jordan Lee (author): Yes—canonicalize is order-only. Added tests to verify decision stability across permutations, plus snapshot tests for known payloads. For Console, it comes back as `status=failed` with `failure_code=GATING_INPUT_INVALID` and `details` listing the first offending metric triple; the UI should show “Internal validation error” (we already map this to “Contact support / rerun” in pilot). I can add a note to the UI mapping ticket if needed.

Benji Okafor (review): Prefer sorting to be explicit about slice_key being optional. Right now undefined sorts before empty string; is that intentional?

Jordan Lee (author): Good call. Updated comparator to normalize slice_key to "" (empty) for ordering only, but still preserve null/undefined in the canonical payload. Also added a test covering undefined vs empty string.

Leila Farouk (review): The randomized-order test uses Math.random; can we seed it so it’s not flaky?

Jordan Lee (author): Updated to a seeded PRNG (xorshift32) so it’s deterministic across runs.

CI: - build (pass) - lint (pass) - unit tests (pass) - integration tests (pass) - policy-engine determinism suite (pass)

Merged: Squash merged to main.
commits: policy-engine: canonicalize gating metrics and use stable ordering in threshold evaluation
policy-engine: add gating metrics schema validator + structured error code
tests: seeded permutation test for deterministic decisions + hash stability
integration: assert stable gating summary hash in apply-flow E2E
